description: Metallic-cascade collapse energetics: latent heat of the silver (Borromean→CFL) crossing per baryon, cascade energy for collapsing cores, comparison with the observed SN 1987A budget, #2074 parity-class bookkeeping of the pre/post composition, and the delayed-second-burst discriminator between the shallow and deep q↔ρ maps.

latent_heat_silver.note: branch gap of prop:borromean-hopf-energy-crossover evaluated AT q = δ_silver; Skein→MeV via the m_p anchor (1 Skein = 1.2570341 MeV)

sn1987a_observed.neutrino_burst_erg: 2e53–5e53 (≈3e53 central; ~13 s; Kamiokande-II 11 + IMB 8 + Baksan 5 events)
sn1987a_observed.standard_attribution: gravitational binding energy of the proto-neutron star (~3/5 GM²/R with relativistic corrections ≈ 3e53 erg), radiated as neutrinos of all flavors

budget_comparison.full_core_cascade_vs_neutrino_burst: 5.737e+52 erg (1.4 M☉ cascade) vs ~3e53 erg observed — the cascade is ~20% of the standard gravitational-binding budget: an ADDITIVE QOU contribution currently hidden inside the factor-~2 uncertainty of the 25-event 1987A sample
budget_comparison.discriminator: a future galactic SN with O(10⁴) detected neutrinos resolves a 20% excess; the sharper signature is the second-burst TIMING structure (below)

scenario_split.shallow_maps_C: heaviest proto-NS cross silver → delayed second ν̄_e burst + ~6e52 erg/M☉ extra; ordinary SNe below the rung show NO excess
scenario_split.deep_maps_A_B: no SN core ever crosses silver (ρ_c ≥ 64 ρ0): cascade fires only inside BH-forming collapse, energy swallowed by the horizon → prediction: NO second burst in any SN; consistent with non-detection to date

second_burst.mechanism: under Map C the proto-NS central density crosses ρ(δ_silver) a few hundred ms after bounce as the core deleptonizes and contracts; the crossing is FIRST-ORDER (Milnor μ̄(123): 1→0, conj:color-superconductivity-borromean) ⇒ a micro-collapse + second shock + second ν̄_e-dominated burst — the same observable shape as the QCD-phase-transition mechanism of Sagert et al. 2009 (arXiv:0809.4225) / Dasgupta et al. 2009 (0912.2568)
second_burst.detectability: few ×10⁵² erg released on ~ms timescale, ν̄_e-dominated: clearly resolvable by IceCube/Super-K/Hyper-K for a galactic event (the corpus's strangelet-merger block already cites ~50 Mpc reach for 2.4e51 erg bursts)

after_collapse.species: proto-neutron star: bulk neutron-rich matter (n + ~10% p,e); under the shallow q↔ρ maps the inner core is past the silver rung: Hopf-diquark (CFL) condensate

neutronization_step.reaction: e⁻ + p → n + ν_e  (Z → Z−1 at fixed A)
neutronization_step.parity_effect: flips Z parity ⇒ at A ≡ 0 (mod 4) it moves a nucleus OUT of the #2074 spectrally-positive class (e.g. ⁵⁶Fe (0,even) allowed → ⁵⁶Mn (0,odd) disallowed): in QOU terms the e-capture cascade forces the matter out of the nuclear admissible classes into bulk braid restructuring
neutronization_step.caveat: the parity class flags spectral positivity (structural admissibility), NOT a lifetime ordering — ⁵⁶Ni (allowed) decays faster than ⁵⁶Co (disallowed); exploratory cross-link only

steady_release.observed: light curve = ⁵⁶Ni → ⁵⁶Co → ⁵⁶Fe radioactive chain (6.1 d / 77.2 d), NOT core physics; late-time NS cooling is core physics
steady_release.qou_reading: post-cascade CFL remnant cools with the gap Δ_CFL ≈ 2.5 MeV suppressing ν emission below T ≈ 2.9e10 K (prop:cfl-neutron-star-observables cooling plateau) — the 'strong steady release' phase

limitations: only the silver rung has a corpus-defined latent heat (Borromean−Hopf branch gap); φ and φ² crossings are not modeled (no corpus EOS for hyperonic/gCFL branch jumps)
cascade energy assumes EVERY baryon in M_core crosses; partial crossings scale linearly
SN 1987A numbers are standard-literature values, not corpus outputs
parity-class bookkeeping is an exploratory cross-link to the #2074 closed form, not a stability claim
